chapter: Hometown ties, community and favorite players
title: Saxophone players he admired
summary: David Jones, Son Johnson, Handy, Bostic, Guy Kelly and Herman Franklin.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I only got the news. Yeah. He's dead. Yeah. And what about saxophone players then? Do they have any good saxophone players?
Well, David Jones was the most outstanding saxophone player. Back in those times you're talking about.
Yeah, wasn't he just 1925 that time?

Yeah, Professor David Jones. Oh. Then you had Hanny. Hanny was of his time. Mm-hmm. Then you had another fellow by the name of Edgar Solskjaer. Mm-hmm. Then you had Son Johnson. Mm-hmm. But Son Johnson was about to, in the later years to come, he was about to, was the greatest saxophone club we had here. They say he really has a big tone. Yeah.
Still got it. Yeah. Well, he and Handy Buck on that job?
Yeah. But, uh, my, my theory, Handy was never no match for him.
Handy wasn't even a match for Earl Bostick.
Earl Bostick stayed around here a long time. Yeah. He was a great saxophone player. Mm-hmm. Gilbert Young was pretty nice during his days. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Ikelly. Ever go to Guy Kelly?
I've heard him on record. How you like him? Oh, he was fine. I never heard Herman Franklin. I met him, but I never heard him.

Well, he was with King Oliver. He stayed with King Oliver until King Oliver died. He was with Celestan too for a while. Yeah, I know. He came with Celestan. He was with Celestan before King Oliver died. Now, after King Oliver died, he came back to Celestan.
